children: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT, Financials), the software and cloud giant behind Azure, is planning a massive expansion for a simple reason: it does not have enough computing capacity.
The company aims to grow its global data-center footprint to more than 38 gigawatts by 2032, up from about 12 gigawatts today, according to a Bloomberg report.
That is more than a threefold increase. And Microsoft already has evidence that it needs it.

Server shortages have reportedly forced the company to turn away some cloud and AI customers. Temu moved a major cloud deal to Oracle after Microsoft could not provide enough capacity in the regions it wanted.

The strain has also reached existing services. GitHub suffered an eight-hour outage in August that was tied to server constraints, while Microsoft has placed limits on Xbox cloud-gaming usage. AI is a big part of what comes next.
Microsoft currently has about 2 gigawatts dedicated to AI. By 2032, AI capacity is expected to represent roughly one-third of the planned 38-gigawatt footprint. That expansion will be expensive.

For investors, the question is whether Microsoft can build fast enough without ending up with too much capacity later. Right now, though, the bigger risk appears to be the opposite: demand is arriving faster than Microsoft can serve it.

title: Microsoft Targets 38GW Data Center Buildout as AI Capacity Crunch Bites
